Bishops' Wars.fact: On the march north, lack of supplies meant they looted the areas they passed through, creating widespread disorder; several units murdered officers suspected of being Catholics, then deserted.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: Lord Conway, the _____ commander in the north, focused on reinforcing Berwick-upon-Tweed, the usual starting point for invading England
Bishops' Wars.fact: The English troops consisted largely of militia from Southern England, poorly-equipped, unpaid, and unenthusiastic about the war. Lord Conway, the English commander in the north, focused on reinforcing Berwick-upon-Tweed, the usual starting point for invading England.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: On 17 _____, cavalry units under Montrose crossed the River Tweed, followed by the rest of Leslie's army
Bishops' Wars.fact: On 17 August, cavalry units under Montrose crossed the River Tweed, followed by the rest of Leslie's army. On 28 August, the Scots forced a passage over the River Tyne at the Battle of Newburn; they still had to take Newcastle, but to Leslie's surprise, when they arrived on 30 August, Conway had withdrawn to Durham.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: The Scots bypassed the town, and headed for _____-upon-Tyne, centre of the coal trade with London, and a valuable bargaining point
Bishops' Wars.fact: The Scots bypassed the town, and headed for Newcastle-upon-Tyne, centre of the coal trade with London, and a valuable bargaining point. On 28 August, the Scots forced a passage over the River Tyne at the Battle of Newburn; they still had to take Newcastle, but to Leslie's surprise, when they arrived on 30 August, Conway had withdrawn to Durham.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: The only other significant action of the war was the siege of _____, held by the Royalist commander Sir Patrick Ruthven, who had previously served with Leslie in the Swedish army
Bishops' Wars.fact: The only other significant action of the war was the siege of Edinburgh Castle, held by the Royalist commander Sir Patrick Ruthven, who had previously served with Leslie in the Swedish army.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: Blockaded since the end of May, starvation forced him to surrender in _____
Bishops' Wars.fact: Blockaded since the end of May, starvation forced him to surrender in September.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: The so-called Long Parliament that assembled in November _____ asserted its power by executing Strafford in May 1641
Bishops' Wars.fact: The so-called Long Parliament that assembled in November 1640 asserted its power by executing Strafford in May 1641.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: By August, the _____ of London was signed and the Scottish army finally evacuated Northern England
Bishops' Wars.fact: By August, the Treaty of London was signed and the Scottish army finally evacuated Northern England.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: Victory confirmed _____ control of government and the Kirk, and Scottish policy now focused on securing these achievements
Bishops' Wars.fact: Victory confirmed Covenanter control of government and the Kirk, and Scottish policy now focused on securing these achievements. The 1643 Solemn League and Covenant was driven by concern over the implications for Scotland if Parliament were defeated; like Charles, the Covenanters sought political power through the creation of a unified church of Scotland and England, only one that was Presbyterian, rather than Episcopalian.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: One of their most prominent opponents was _____, who claimed he would fight rather than agree to such an outcome
Bishops' Wars.fact: One of their most prominent opponents was Oliver Cromwell, who claimed he would fight rather than agree to such an outcome.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: The so-called _____ that assembled in November 1640 asserted its power by executing Strafford in May 1641
Bishops' Wars.fact: The so-called Long Parliament that assembled in November 1640 asserted its power by executing Strafford in May 1641.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: Their retreat further lowered _____ morale, while the Scots now felt confident enough to ignore the 10 mile limit, and on 5 June advanced as far as Duns
Bishops' Wars.fact: Encountering Scottish units, the English feared they were outnumbered, and retreated back across the border without a shot being fired. Their retreat further lowered English morale, while the Scots now felt confident enough to ignore the 10 mile limit, and on 5 June advanced as far as Duns.

Bishops' Wars.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bishops' Wars.question: His advisors convinced _____ the only way to finance a second war was to recall the English Parliament, and in December 1639, he issued writs for the first time since 1629
Bishops' Wars.fact: When Charles' representative, Lord Traquair, tried to suspend it, his action was declared illegal and Parliament continued to sit. His advisors convinced Charles the only way to finance a second war was to recall the English Parliament, and in December 1639, he issued writs for the first time since 1629.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: The _____ was Ring on the side of a horse's bit.
Bit ring.fact: The bit ring is the ring on the side of a horse's bit, particularly on a snaffle bit.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Size and _____ of the Rings: Rings are generally 2–5 inches in diameter, most commonly ranging in the 2.5–3 inch range that is legal for horse show competition
Bit ring.fact: Size and Thickness of the Rings: Rings are generally 2–5 inches in diameter, most commonly ranging in the 2.5–3 inch range that is legal for horse show competition. Thickness ranges from 10 to 23 mm, with most found at 15 mm.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Size and _____ of Rings: The rings range from rounder and thinner to wider and flatter in shape
Bit ring.fact: Size and Thickness of Rings: The rings range from rounder and thinner to wider and flatter in shape. Their thickness varies from 10-23mm, and most are about 3" across.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Uses: _____ are overall one of the most popular ring designs, less common in the dressage arena than loose-rings, more often seen in show hunter disciplines
Bit ring.fact: Uses: Eggbutts are overall one of the most popular ring designs, less common in the dressage arena than loose-rings, more often seen in show hunter disciplines. Eggbutts are sometimes seen in eventing, show jumping, and equitation riding.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Size and _____ of the Rings: The ring is usually about 3" in width, although they may reach 5" (a popular size for race horses, but illegal for horse shows)
Bit ring.fact: Size and Thickness of the Rings: Rings are generally 2–5 inches in diameter, most commonly ranging in the 2.5–3 inch range that is legal for horse show competition. Thickness ranges from 10 to 23 mm, with most found at 15 mm.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Size and Thickness of the Rings: Rings are generally 2–_____ in diameter, most commonly ranging in the 2.5–3 inch range that is legal for horse show competition
Bit ring.fact: Size and Thickness of the Rings: Rings are generally 2–5 inches in diameter, most commonly ranging in the 2.5–3 inch range that is legal for horse show competition.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Mouthpiece: comes in many mouthpiece sizes, with 5" being the most standard size for the average horse, with a range from 3" for miniature horses to over _____ for a large warmblood or a draft horse
Bit ring.fact: Mouthpiece: comes in many mouthpiece sizes, with 5" being the most standard size for the average horse, with a range from 3" for miniature horses to over 6 inches for a large warmblood or a draft horse.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Mouthpiece: This is also a popular bit that comes in many sizes, ranging from 3–_____
Bit ring.fact: Mouthpiece: This is also a popular bit that comes in many sizes, ranging from 3–6.5 inches.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Uses: _____ very popular design, the Dee-ring was the traditional bit used in hunt seat riding, and is still seen in that discipline
Bit ring.fact: Uses: Another very popular design, the Dee-ring was the traditional bit used in hunt seat riding, and is still seen in that discipline.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Mouthpieces: _____ in all sizes and thickness (10–21 mm)
Bit ring.fact: Mouthpieces: Range in all sizes and thickness (10–21 mm).

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Mouthpieces: _____ varies, Mouthpieces come in all types, except waterfords are rare
Bit ring.fact: Mouthpieces: Size varies, Mouthpieces come in all types, except waterfords are rare.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Advantages: _____ the rotation of the loose ring without as great a chance that the ring will pinch
Bit ring.fact: Advantages: Provides the rotation of the loose ring without as great a chance that the ring will pinch.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Action: _____ has an eggbutt-like ring at the mouthpiece for the rein, with an upper cheek that has a ring at its end, to which the cheekpieces of the bridle are attached
Bit ring.fact: Action: The Baucher has an eggbutt-like ring at the mouthpiece for the rein, with an upper cheek that has a ring at its end, to which the cheekpieces of the bridle are attached.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: The mouthpiece of a true _____ does not slide on its ring, though there are Baucher-like designs that do
Bit ring.fact: Action: The Baucher has an eggbutt-like ring at the mouthpiece for the rein, with an upper cheek that has a ring at its end, to which the cheekpieces of the bridle are attached. The mouthpiece of a true Baucher does not slide on its ring, though there are Baucher-like designs that do.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: NOTE: the _____ can be misused in an upside-down position, with the cheek containing the smaller ring hanging below the bit, as if the reins were supposed to attach at that point
Bit ring.fact: NOTE: the Baucher can be misused in an upside-down position, with the cheek containing the smaller ring hanging below the bit, as if the reins were supposed to attach at that point.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Flat-ring: _____ to the loose-ring, but the circular ring has been flattened so it has edges
Bit ring.fact: Flat-ring: Similar to the loose-ring, but the circular ring has been flattened so it has edges. Has similar action as the loose-ring, though is a little more stable in the horse's mouth and the rings may be less likely to pinch.

Bit ring.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit ring.question: Tubular Butt: _____ to the eggbutt but with a sliding loose-ring and is suitable for use with reins that are connected with various knots
Bit ring.fact: Flat-ring: Similar to the loose-ring, but the circular ring has been flattened so it has edges. Has similar action as the loose-ring, though is a little more stable in the horse's mouth and the rings may be less likely to pinch.

Bit shank.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit shank.question: The _____ was Horse tack.
Bit shank.fact: The bit shank is the side piece or cheekpiece of a curb bit, part of the bridle, used when riding on horses. The bit shank allows leverage to be added to the pressure of the rider's hands on the bit.

Bit shank.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit shank.question: Shanked bits in the curb family include the _____, which is the curb portion of the double bridle; the pelham bit, a single bit ridden with two sets of reins; and the single-reined curb bit
Bit shank.fact: Shanked bits in the curb family include the Weymouth, which is the curb portion of the double bridle; the pelham bit, a single bit ridden with two sets of reins; and the single-reined curb bit.

Bit shank.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit shank.question: Cheek sizes vary from the _____ (about 4½ inches long) to bits that exceed the 8½ inch "show legal" maximum cheek length
Bit shank.fact: Cheek sizes vary from the Tom Thumb (about 4½ inches long) to bits that exceed the 8½ inch "show legal" maximum cheek length.

Bit shank.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bit shank.question: Horses that maintain a more vertical head position, such as dressage horses and western horses trained in the "straight up" or _____ tradition generally use a curb bit with straighter shanks
Bit shank.fact: Horses that maintain a more vertical head position, such as dressage horses and western horses trained in the "straight up" or Vaquero tradition generally use a curb bit with straighter shanks.

Bitbucket.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bitbucket.question: The _____ was Web-based hosting service for software development projects.
Bitbucket.fact: Bitbucket is a Git-based source code repository hosting service owned by Atlassian. Bitbucket offers both commercial plans and free accounts with an unlimited number of private repositories.

Bitbucket.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bitbucket.question: It also provides integration with other _____ tools
Bitbucket.fact: It also provides integration with other Atlassian tools. Atlassian provides Bitbucket Server for free to open source projects meeting certain criteria, and to organizations that are non-profit, non-government, non-academic, non-commercial, non-political, and secular.

Bitbucket.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bitbucket.question: On 29 September _____, Bitbucket was acquired by Atlassian
Bitbucket.fact: On 29 September 2010, Bitbucket was acquired by Atlassian.

Bitbucket.subject: Environment & Ecology
Bitbucket.question: In March _____, Bitbucket Server dropped support for viewing three way diffs and in July 2020, Bitbucket Cloud removed support for its original repository format Mercurial
Bitbucket.fact: In March 2020, Bitbucket Server dropped support for viewing three way diffs and in July 2020, Bitbucket Cloud removed support for its original repository format Mercurial.
